report:
404 in UI when publishing container image with a slash in name

### Description

Publishing a container image than contains a slash `/` to Gitea container registry succeeds, but when trying to view it in UI, I get error 404. The only solution is to go into system preferences and delete package from there (which, thankfully, works).

According to [documentation](https://docs.gitea.com/usage/packages/container), names that contain slash are valid.

Steps to repoduce:

0. Lets say we want to push local image `localhost/someimage` with the name `namespace/name`.
1. Create some Docker image and tag it in the following fashion: `docker tag gitea.example.com/username/namespace/name localhost/someimage`.
2. Push the image with `docker push gitea.example.com/username/namespace/name`.
3. Open web UI. Navigate to Profile -> Packages. You should see the pushed image with the name `namespace/name`.
4. Click on the said image.

**Expected behavior**: package page opens.

**Actual behavior**: 404 page.

### Gitea Version

1.21.10

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Operating System

Linux

### How are you running Gitea?

Self-hosted binary.

### Database

PostgreSQL

evidence.quote: If you access the URL with `%2F` directly, what does Gitea side see (the Gitea logs) ? If Gitea also sees `%2F`, then it is a Gitea's bug. If Gitea only sees `/`, then it is the reverse proxy's problem: it shouldn't decode the path.

confirmation.quote: Gitea sees `/`. And it is, apparently, a reverse proxy problem, as I am running Gitea behind an NGINX proxy. I confirm that without NGINX reverse proxy, the issue does not reproduce. ... Removing the trailing slash in proxy_pass directive fixed the issue.

ambiguity: Reads as a Gitea routing/UI bug for container images with a slash in the name (D), citing docs that such names are valid; B (unsupported naming) is also conceivable. Body says 'Self-hosted binary' and never mentions a reverse proxy; 'cannot reproduce on demo' is the only hint.
decisive_code: routers/web/web.go: package UI routes are m.Group("/{type}/{name}") -> "/{version}", i.e. the name is ONE path segment; models/packages/descriptor.go:PackageWebLink/VersionWebLink build the link with url.PathEscape(pd.Package.LowerName) (so 'namespace/name' becomes 'namespace%2Fname'); modules/context/base.go:Params url.PathUnescape()s the chi param and modules/context/package.go:PackageAssignment looks the package up by that unescaped name (chi routes on RawPath when present). With the escaped URL Gitea resolves the package; a 404 happens only if something upstream decodes %2F into '/', producing an extra segment that no route matches.
notes: nginx 'proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000/;' (trailing slash) normalizes/decodes the URI; twin of gitea-31321 (npm @scope%2Fname), use only one.

reviews.decidable_why: 'Cannot reproduce on demo site' plus self-hosted setup hints at environment, but no mention of a reverse proxy in the body.
The body says 'Self-hosted binary' and never mentions a reverse proxy. From the report alone, a 404 on a slash-containing package name looks like a routing bug.

difficulty_note: The report never mentions a proxy; the class follows only from showing the code handles the input correctly, so the symptom must come from outside (plus the hint that the demo site does not reproduce it).
